verdict: DuPont's slimmed-down business grew sales 4% to $1.9B and raised its full-year outlook, while the businesses it has split off or sold dragged total profit down to $126M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted, continuing ops)
kpis.note: vs $0.70 a year ago; total diluted EPS was $0.91 after discontinued operations

kpis.label: Operating EBITDA
kpis.note: +8% YoY, a 25.1% margin — the company's preferred profit measure, continuing operations

kpis.label: Transaction-adjusted free cash flow
kpis.note: Cash from continuing operations of $410M less $71M of capex (money spent on plants and equipment) and $2M of separation payments; 121% of adjusted earnings

segments.name: Healthcare & Water Technologies
segments.note: Healthcare materials (such as medical packaging and personal protection) and water-treatment products. Sales rose 4% on organic growth — healthcare up mid-single digits, water up low-single digits despite disruption in the Middle East. Operating EBITDA (a profit measure before interest, tax and non-cash charges) was $263M, a 30.4% margin.

segments.name: Diversified Industrials
segments.note: Building materials and industrial products, including aerospace and electric-vehicle battery applications. Sales rose 4% (organic sales up 5%, partly offset by currency). Operating EBITDA was $242M, a 24.1% margin.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Developing new materials and products for healthcare, water and industrial uses. Down from $52M a year ago.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling products and running the company — sales teams, finance, legal and admin. Flat vs a year ago.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: A non-cash charge that spreads the cost of past acquisitions (bought technology and customer relationships) over their useful lives.

opex.name: Restructuring
opex.note: Costs of reshaping the business — job cuts and writing down assets that are no longer needed.

opex.name: Separation costs
opex.note: Acquisition, integration and separation costs — deal and break-up costs — mainly separating the Qnity electronics business and selling the Aramids business. Down sharply from $62M a year ago.

otherDetail: A net $47M cost below operating profit: sundry income of $38M (miscellaneous gains, including interest income), less $40M of interest expense, less the $45M loss from discontinued operations — the Qnity electronics business spun off on Nov 1, 2025 and the Aramids business sold on Apr 1, 2026, both shown net of tax. The flow also adds $5M of equity earnings from part-owned affiliates, shown as its own line in the chart math.

takeaways.title: The kept businesses are growing
takeaways.text: Net sales from continuing operations rose 4% to $1,868M — organic sales (growth excluding currency and deals) rose 5%. Healthcare & Water Technologies grew 4% to $865M and Diversified Industrials grew 4% to $1,003M. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to about $7.19B of sales and $7.47–$7.52 of adjusted EPS.

takeaways.title: Continuing profit jumped 68%
takeaways.text: Income from continuing operations was $171M, up from $102M a year ago, as higher segment earnings met lower interest expense ($40M vs $85M) and much lower separation costs. Continuing diluted EPS was $1.24 vs $0.70; adjusted EPS, which leaves out one-offs and amortization, was $2.09.

takeaways.title: The total bottom line is smaller than the continuing one
takeaways.text: Total net income was $126M — $123M of it attributable to DuPont shareholders — because discontinued operations (Qnity and Aramids) lost $45M after tax. That gap is the clean-up cost of the break-up, not the performance of the business DuPont kept.

oneTimers: Discontinued operations lost $45M after tax in the quarter. These are the businesses DuPont has exited — the Qnity electronics spin-off (completed Nov 1, 2025) and the Aramids sale (completed Apr 1, 2026, for about $1.2B cash plus a $300M note and a stake in the buyer) — so their results no longer count as continuing operations.

Continuing operations include $15M of acquisition, integration and separation costs and $6M of restructuring and asset-related charges before tax ($22M of significant items in total, plus a $43M one-off tax charge inside the $108M tax line). A year ago the same separation costs were $62M, so this drag is fading.
footerNote: All figures are on a continuing-operations basis (after the Qnity spin-off and Aramids sale); amounts are reported in $M and tie exactly.
follow100Note: Total net income of $126M includes the $45M discontinued-operations loss; $123M was attributable to DuPont shareholders after $3M for noncontrolling interests. Tax of $108M is the tax on continuing operations; discontinued operations are shown net of tax inside other income/expense.
